post.title: When the Job Goes, the Housing Follows: ICESCR Article 11 and the Living Standard Gap
key_claims: ICESCR Article 11 recognizes the right to adequate food, clothing, housing, and continuous improvement of living conditions (treaty text)
CESCR GC 4 (1991) defines adequate housing across 7 criteria including affordability and accessibility
CESCR GC 12 (1999) defines adequate food through availability, accessibility, adequacy, and sustainability
Algorithmic tenant screening systems disadvantage gig/platform workers via income-documentation requirements designed for W-2 employment — structural inference, not a published CESCR finding
AI displacement into gig arrangements creates income volatility that undermines housing and food accessibility under GC 4/GC 12 standards
